messages:
incidence-bot: [P0] Paging on-call: Aurora (enterprise / VPC) — abnormal SSE/websocket reconnects and increased 5xx from customer app gateway. Rule: appgw_stream_errors > 50/min. Linked alerts: grafana/r/aurora-appgw-streaming. Pager URL: https://pager.example/PD12345

oncall-ashley: acked — I’m on call. Paging infra & runtime. @marta @samir can you triage pool + routing?

marta: looking. preliminary: I see spike in connection resets from aurora tenant (tenant_id=aurora-42) starting ~22:03 UTC. Dedicated pool "ded-aurora-42" CPU high, connections 9k (normal ~2k). Possible thundering herd from client reconnects.

samir: hypotheses: 1) upstream appgw is retrying too aggressively causing conn churn; 2) our KV cache pressure causing evictions and longer tail latencies => gateway timeouts. Will check runtime logs.

jordan-customer: we started seeing 502/504 at ~22:02. sample from their gateway logs: ```
[2026-03-14T22:04:11Z] conn=12456 req_id=aa12 upstream=10.1.2.5:5043 GET /sse/stream x-retries=3 socket_err=ECONNRESET
[2026-03-14T22:04:12Z] conn=12457 req_id=aa13 upstream=10.1.2.6:5043 GET /sse/stream x-retries=2 upstream_resp=502
```

oncall-ashley: impact check: Jordan, are user-visible reconnections causing data loss or just degraded UX? any SLA hits reported?

jordan-customer: mostly degraded UX — clients reconnect and receive duplicate events sometimes. Some long-poll fallback logging in client. No revenue-impacting workflows yet but they see ~18% of sessions reconnecting.

marta: running quick pool inspect: ```
# redwoodctl pool inspect ded-aurora-42 --json | jq '.connections, .cpu_pct, .memory_pct'
9000
86
71
```
We can burst scale 2 nodes from pool autoscaler but need approval (reserved capacity).

samir: runtime trace snippet showing KV miss spike and tail latency: ```
trace_id=trs-8a7 latency_p50=45ms p99=1.8s kv_hits=12% kv_misses=88% concurrent_requests=2400
```
If KV cache thrash is true, that can exacerbate SSE stitching and cause upstream timeouts. Two mitigations: increase cache memory for that pool (quick config) OR temporarily route aurora traffic to a compatible model variant with smaller KV working set.

oncall-ashley: both sound viable. Priorities: 1) reduce client reconnects (customer-side and gateway retry), 2) reduce load on runtime. Actions: marta, can you request +2 nodes burst? samir, can you open hotfix routing to degrade to polling or lower-state variant? I'll coordinate with customer and sales.

marta: Requesting burst now: `redwoodctl autoscale request --pool ded-aurora-42 --add-nodes 2 --reason "SSE reconnect storm"` — submitted, ETA ~90s.

kate-sales: looping in AM and customer success: @jordan-customer I’ll help communicate ETA and workaround guidance to the Aurora ops team.

samir: opened temporary route in routing service: ```
# routingctl set-policy --tenant aurora-42 --policy "sse->fallback-polling" --ttl 30m
Applied policy: fallback polling enabled for aurora-42, TTL 30m
```
This will inject X-RW-Stream: disable header at edge to force polling. Push staged in 10s.

ops-bot: grafana snapshot: https://grafana.example/d-snapshot/aurora-20260314-2206 (error rate x6, conn count x4). Trending: reconnect spikes align with client retries.

jordan-customer: we can lower client retry count on our side. Pushing patch to mobile/web SDK to backoff faster. ETA ~15m.

marta: autoscale completed — pool +2 nodes in 75s. Post-scale metrics: connections 5.2k, cpu 48%. Looks effective at reducing queuing.

samir: routing fallback is live. Early signs: reconnects dropped from 18% -> 7% in first 2 min. KV miss rate still elevated but absolute concurrent requests dropped ~40%.

oncall-ashley: good. Next steps: 1) keep fallback routing for 30m while customer deploys client fix; 2) keep burst nodes for 2h and reevaluate; 3) schedule follow-up post-incident to tune per-tenant connection limiter and retry logic. Who owns post-incident?

marta: I’ll own infra action item to add per-tenant soft connection limit and alert when >3k connections growth in 5m.

samir: I’ll own runtime change to expose per-tenant KV working set metrics and recommend quantization profile for aurora workload.

kate-sales: I’ll coordinate postmortem call with Aurora PO and CS.

jordan-customer: thanks — applying client backoff now. We’ll keep you posted.

oncall-ashley: closing immediate P0 mitigation checklist — routing fallback + autoscale + customer client patch. Will keep this thread as the coordination channel. If anything regresses, re-page. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: annotation: incident tag "aurora-vpc-sse-20260314" created. Timeline recorded.

samir: note for post-incident: consider adding an automatic graceful-degrade policy for enterprise VPCs where streaming errors + conn spike => auto-enable polling fallback and soft-scale. Might avoid manual steps next time.

jordan-customer: verified on device fleet: reconnects down to 4% after client patch. Thank you all.

oncall-ashley: thanks team — monitoring for 30m then hand off to follow-up owners.

incidence-bot: SYSTEM: Incident status changed -> mitigated by routing fallback + pool scale. Severity downgraded to SEV2 at 22:28 UTC. Metrics: error-rate normalized to baseline.
